items.followUp: What makes an algorithm explainable, and what can it tell a user about its result?

rubric.why: Captures the defining idea that people can understand the algorithm’s working or decisions.
rubric.description: Defines an explainable algorithm as one whose working or decisions can be understood by humans.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that humans can understand the algorithm’s working or decisions.

rubric.why: States that the algorithm can clarify the reason for its result.
rubric.description: Explains that it helps show how or why a particular result was produced.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing an explanation of the algorithm’s result or decision.

modelAnswer: An explainable algorithm is an algorithm whose working and decisions can be understood by humans.
It helps show how or why the algorithm produced a particular result.

items.followUp: How does two-factor authentication provide an extra layer of security?

rubric.why: Identifies that access requires two verification steps or factors.
rubric.description: Defines 2FA as a method requiring two forms of verification to access an account.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that two forms of verification are required.

rubric.why: Gives a valid example of two different authentication factors.
rubric.description: Provides an example such as a password followed by a one-time code.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving a valid pair of authentication factors.

modelAnswer: Two-factor authentication (2FA) is a security method that requires two forms of verification to access an account.
For example, a user may enter a password and then provide a one-time code sent to their phone.

items.followUp: State one way e-mail marketing can help a business reach customers.

rubric.why: Identifies e-mail as the channel and promotional messages as the content.
rubric.description: Defines e-mail marketing as sending commercial or promotional messages by e-mail.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying promotional or commercial messages sent by e-mail.

rubric.why: Explains the business purpose of those messages.
rubric.description: States that businesses use e-mail marketing to advertise products or services to customers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the use of e-mail to promote products or services.

modelAnswer: E-mail marketing is the use of e-mail to send commercial or promotional messages to customers.
Businesses use it to advertise their products or services and communicate with customers.

items.followUp: Describe the main components of the Von Neumann architecture and state their functions.

rubric.why: Identifies the stored-program concept and that instructions and data share memory.
rubric.description: States that the architecture stores instructions and data in the same memory.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the stored-program concept and shared memory.

rubric.why: States the storage function of the memory unit.
rubric.description: Explains that the memory unit stores the data and instructions needed by the computer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the memory unit’s storage function.

rubric.why: Identifies the CPU’s Control Unit and ALU and their functions.
rubric.description: Names the Control Unit and ALU, describing the Control Unit’s direction of operations and the ALU’s arithmetic and logical operations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both units and describing their roles.

rubric.why: Explains how data enters and results leave the computer.
rubric.description: States that input units enter data and output units present results.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing both input and output functions.

modelAnswer: The Von Neumann architecture uses the stored-program concept: instructions and data are kept in the same memory.
The memory unit stores the data and instructions needed by the computer.
The CPU contains the Control Unit, which directs operations, and the ALU, which performs arithmetic and logical operations.
Input units enter data and instructions, while output units present the results.

items.followUp: Describe any four layers of the OSI model and state the function of each.

rubric.why: Identifies the Physical layer and its role in transmitting bits over a medium.
rubric.description: Physical layer: transmits raw bits through the physical communication medium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and stating its bit-transmission function.

rubric.why: Identifies the Data Link layer’s handling of frames.
rubric.description: Data Link layer: organizes data into frames and manages communication between directly connected devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and describing framing or link communication.

rubric.why: Identifies the Network layer’s packet-routing role.
rubric.description: Network layer: routes packets between networks using logical addresses.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and describing routing or logical addressing.

rubric.why: Identifies the Transport layer’s end-to-end delivery role.
rubric.description: Transport layer: provides end-to-end delivery of data between devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and describing end-to-end delivery.

modelAnswer: Physical layer: transmits raw bits over the physical communication medium.
Data Link layer: organizes data into frames and manages communication between directly connected devices.
Network layer: routes packets between networks using logical addresses.
Transport layer: provides end-to-end delivery of data between devices.

items.followUp: Explain four ways digital technologies can help an entrepreneur start or grow a business.

rubric.why: Explains how digital technology helps promote a business and reach customers.
rubric.description: Online marketing helps entrepreneurs promote products and reach potential customers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing online promotion or increased customer reach.

rubric.why: Identifies online selling as a business opportunity enabled by technology.
rubric.description: E-commerce allows a business to sell products or services through online platforms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning online sales or e-commerce.

rubric.why: Recognizes that digital tools can improve business operations.
rubric.description: Digital tools can automate tasks and improve operational efficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing automation or improved efficiency.

rubric.why: Explains how business data can inform decisions and understanding of customers.
rubric.description: Data analysis helps entrepreneurs understand customers and make informed business decisions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking data analysis to customer understanding or decision-making.

modelAnswer: Digital technologies allow entrepreneurs to market their products online and reach more customers.
E-commerce enables them to sell products and services through online platforms.
Digital tools can automate business tasks and improve operational efficiency.
Data analysis helps entrepreneurs understand customers and make informed business decisions.
